_meta.purpose: Identifies the actual school districts behind the abbreviated codes already in tax-districts-fy2025-26.json (School 2CJ, School 17-C, School CC 1, ESD, SWOCC), for use in a drill-down view. Cross-references to the existing property-tax data -- does not duplicate it.

k12_districts.history_note: Formed in 1997 when four elementary districts (including the former Ophir and Pistol River elementary districts) and one high school district merged into a single K-12 district.

k12_districts.enrollment_note: One of Oregon's smallest districts -- roughly 230-300 K-12 students district-wide as of recent years.

k12_districts.history_note: Formed in 1950 when the Brookings and Harbor districts consolidated.
k12_districts.current_news_note: As of the FY2025-26 data collection date, the district has a school bond measure (Measure 8-118) on the May 2026 ballot for facility repairs/upgrades, which if passed would add roughly $0.55 per $1,000 assessed value and bring about $6.1 million in Oregon School Capital Improvement Matching (OSCIM) state funds. This is separate from and additional to the current School 17-C tax rate already in tax-districts-fy2025-26.json -- do not include it in current-year totals, but it may be worth a 'heads up, this could change' note in the app.

regional_education_entities.official_name: South Coast Education Service District (likely -- verify)
regional_education_entities.note: ESD in the tax rate data covers all of Curry County uniformly (rate applies to the full assessed value base, not split by sub-district). Education Service Districts in Oregon provide shared regional services (special education support, technology, professional development) to the K-12 districts within their boundary, rather than running their own schools directly.
Community college district. Also applies uniformly across the full Curry County tax base. Not K-12 -- offers 2-year degrees, workforce training, and transfer credit toward 4-year colleges.

already_sourced_facts.fact: Oregon's Common School Fund -- generated from state-managed school trust lands, not property tax -- distributed $57,779 to Central Curry School District in 2025, as part of a statewide $76.8 million distribution to all Oregon districts.
already_sourced_facts.relevance: Good example of a genuinely non-property-tax, non-state-School-Fund source -- a third funding stream worth mentioning in a 'where does the rest of the money come from' explainer.
